chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Al-Sabbah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) conquered Khaybar, he left it in their hands upon a stipulation of half. So when the fruit reached maturity, he sent Abdullah ibn Rawahah to them, who evaluated it for them. So they came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him,
He has increased (the estimation) upon us.

So he sent a message to Abdullah, and he said: 'What are they saying?' He said, 'I had evaluated upon them with something, so if they so desire to they can take with what we have evaluated, and if they so desire to, we take it'. So a man from the Jews said, 'By this (justice) stand the skies and the earth'.

key_terms.النِّصْفِ: Half (referring to the share of produce)

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling regarding the land of Khaybar after its conquest and how was the produce shared?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) administrative decision to retain the Jewish tribes of Khaybar on their lands under a half-share lease (*kharaj*), establishing a precedent for Islamic land tenure and agricultural contracts. The narrative highlights the role of Abdullah ibn Rawahah as a trusted evaluator (*kharis*) and underscores the principle of fairness in valuation, which the Jewish respondent acknowledged as foundational to cosmic order. This event is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding *khums* and the rights of landowners under Islamic governance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, from Abu Al Sabbah who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that when the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> conquered Khyber, he<sup>saww</sup> left it in their hands upon a stipulation that the half (would be for each party). So when the fruits reached (maturity), he<sup>saww</sup> sent Abdullah in Rawahat to them, who evaluated it upon them. So they came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and they said to him<sup>saww</sup>,

So he<sup>saww</sup> sent a message to Abdullah, and he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What are they saying?’ He said, ‘I had evaluated upon them with something, so if they so desire to they can take with what we have evaluated, and if they so desire to, we take it’. So a man from the Jews said, ‘By this (justice) stand the skies and the earth’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from abu al-Sabbah who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘When the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, liberated Khaybar he left it in their hand for half. When fruits ripened he (the Messenger of Allah) delegated ‘Abd Allah ibn Rawahah who estimated the value and they came to the Holy Prophet, and said, ‘He has charged us more.’

He (the Messenger of Allah) sent someone to ask ‘Abd Allah if there was reason for which they complained. He replied, ‘I estimated and they can take or we take it.’ A Jewish man then said, ‘This is (justice) the fact upon which the skies and earth are maintained.’”
